item.title: Warm Music for Morning Tips

turns.text: Add some warm, hopeful music to this clip, nothing too energetic. Keep the whole video and my voice.

item.tests: Tests whether the delivered video adds music matching an explicit mood while preserving the source footage and speech.

answer_sheet.Music mood: Warm and hopeful, with gentle energy rather than a driving beat.
answer_sheet.Footage and length: Use the entire attached 10-second clip without changing its visuals or timing.
answer_sheet.Original audio: Keep my original voice audible and understandable.
answer_sheet.Platform, framing, and added text: Keep the original framing. No added text; no particular platform.

must_haves: The output contains the full original 10-second kitchen-table video, with no new shots or altered playback speed.
Added music is clearly audible and has a warm, hopeful, gentle character rather than an aggressive or high-energy feel.
The woman's original spoken introduction remains audible and understandable throughout.
The added music ends with the video rather than continuing over extra footage or a blank screen.

turns.text: Could you add some music to the clip I've attached? I've been going back and forth about asking for help with this because I tend to overthink these little things. Please keep the whole video and my voice. For the music, I mean something warm and hopeful, but nothing too energetic. I'm excited to see how it feels with music underneath it.

dialog.agent:
Warm, hopeful, and gentle sounds like a good fit—soft piano with a little ambient texture, kept low beneath your voice.

One limitation: the connected tools can generate a music track, but they can’t mix it into your existing clip while preserving the full video and original voice. I haven’t changed your clip.

If a separate instrumental track would help, tell me the clip’s duration and I can make one to match, ready to add underneath your voice in a video editor.
dialog.why: It states that the connected tools cannot mix music into the existing clip while preserving the video and voice, and confirms the clip was not changed. It offers a separate track as an alternative.
dialog.user: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

dialog.agent:
I can try making the music separately; I still can’t mix it into the clip with these tools. Your full video and voice will stay untouched.

How long should it be?
dialog.why: It asks how long the music should be and waits for the user's input.
dialog.user: It should be 10 seconds, to match the entire attached clip. Yes, please go ahead with the separate music track, keeping it warm and hopeful with gentle energy rather than a driving beat. When it goes underneath the clip, I still want my original voice to be audible and understandable.

dialog.agent:
The music generator has a **15-second minimum**, so I can’t request exactly 10 seconds. Would a 15-second instrumental that you can trim to fit be okay?

I’d keep it warm and hopeful, with soft textures, no vocals, and no driving beat. When you add it, keep its volume low beneath your original voice so every word stays clear.
dialog.why: It asks whether a 15-second instrumental would be acceptable instead of 10 seconds and waits for the user’s choice.
dialog.user: Yes, please go ahead with the 15-second instrumental, and I can trim it to fit the 10-second clip. Warm and hopeful with gentle energy sounds right, and I’m happy to leave the instrumentation to you. I still want to keep the entire video unchanged, with my voice audible and understandable.

turns.agent:
I tried to generate the 15-second instrumental, but Magic Hour refused the request because your account has insufficient credits. **No music was created, and your video and voice remain unchanged.**

Here’s the music direction ready to reuse when credits are available:

> Warm, hopeful instrumental underscore with soft piano and subtle ambient pads. Gentle, relaxed energy, no vocals, no driving beat, and no sudden swells. Sparse enough to sit beneath speech without competing with it.

Once added, trim the music—not the video—to 10 seconds and keep it low beneath your voice.
